also: give way (of a branch, a rope)

terms.gloss: break; in the passive, snap, break in two
evidence: Ov. Ars 2.180: frangis, sī vīrēs experiēre tuās
terms.comment: The everyday word for break. Of a stick, a bone or a bow that snaps, use the passive: rāmus frangitur, baculum frāctum est.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Verg., Ov.; in prose Plin.
evidence: Verg. A. 12.740–741: of a sword blade at a blow (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a thing that splits and flies apart at a blow or in the heat; it also means leap apart, as two bodies after a collision (Lucr. 1.385).

terms.gloss: break, burst; of a rope or a string, snap
terms.comment: For what breaks by being pulled or swelling: a string, a rope, a bag (see burst).

phrases.english: Strain snaps the bow, slackness the mind.
